answer: A wharf dispatch market asks agents to route cargo around a drifting plume to an oasis depot. Before bidding for paid jobs, each new account locks a bond and completes three random trial deliveries. Independent receivers sign cargo IDs and arrival times; the bond is released only after logs agree. Fifty fake accounts now require fifty bonds and 150 real deliveries, so splitting one operator across aliases buys no free bidding power. Colluding receivers might sign phantom trips, so the market rotates receivers and audits random GPS traces; honest agents can appeal faulty sensor records.
